title: Building Accessible Tabs & Accordions 📑
description: Apply ARIA to create a fully keyboard-navigable tab panel and an accordion component.

slides.title: The Tab Pattern 🗂️
slides.content:
Tabs are a common UI pattern. Accessible tabs need:

* `role="tablist"` on the container.
* `role="tab"` on each tab trigger (should be `<button>`).
* `role="tabpanel"` on each content panel.
* `aria-selected` on the active tab.
* Keyboard navigation: arrow keys move between tabs; Tab moves into the active panel.

options.text: Tab between tabs, Enter to select
Arrow keys move between tabs; Tab moves into the active panel

quizData.explanation: Per ARIA Authoring Practices, Left/Right arrows cycle tabs, while Tab focuses the active panel content.

slides.title: The Accordion Pattern 📂
slides.content:
An accordion is a series of disclosure buttons that each control a collapsible region.

* Each header is a `<button>` (or element with `role="button"`).
* `aria-expanded` on the button indicates the panel state.
* `aria-controls` links the button to its panel ID (optional but good).
* The panel uses `role="region"` and has an accessible name (often `aria-labelledby` the button).

Multiple panels can be open at once – not mutually exclusive like tabs.

quizData.question: Which state attribute must change when an accordion panel opens or closes?
quizData.explanation: `aria-expanded` signals to assistive tech whether the controlled region is visible.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Keep it Simple: Use `<details>` and `<summary>`
HTML5 provides a native disclosure widget with full semantics. For simple accordions, you may not need ARIA at all.
